Hi Jonathan / Asha 
- thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we're aligned before Dylan follows up with technical estimates:

Summary of requirements (please confirm):
- Expected workflows: contextual summarization + answer generation on customer documents. Hybrid read-heavy prompts (avg input tokens ~1200) and concise generated outputs (avg 400 tokens).
- Context window: you may expand up to 8k for select use cases but initial pilot will use 2k.
- Latency SLO: target p95 <= 350 ms for the full request (input+generation) on the 2k context pilot.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline 60 QPS sustained, burst up to 200 QPS; concurrency per model endpoint ~50 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: yes — you want streaming responses (time-to-first-token matters).

Action items / next steps:
1) Dylan will provide per-context-window latency estimates and recommended configuration (model family, quantization, batching strategy, Dedicated vs Hosted).
2) I'll set up a 2-week dedicated perf trial (we can reserve a Dedicated node or run a hosted perf lab depending on your preference).
3) Please share any additional test data (anonymized) and a short list of peak-hour windows so we can simulate bursts.

Attachments: redwood-latency-sla-appendix.pdf (SLA language + example configs)

If any of the bullets above don't match what you expect, flag them and I'll update. Otherwise, expect a technical follow-up from Dylan by tomorrow morning PST.

Best,

Thanks Marissa 
- that lines up with our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 350 ms p95 is for the 2k context pilot. For 8k context (later phase) we'd accept up to 700 ms p95 but want clear visibility into degradation.
- Throughput: 60 QPS sustained is the baseline; bursting to 200 QPS could occur for brief campaigns (5-10 minutes).
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent requests per endpoint is accurate; we may split across two endpoints for redundancy.
- Streaming: high priority. Time-to-first-token should be minimized (ideally <80 ms) for the interactive flows.

We can share a small sample dataset for testing — attaching a sanitized transcripts bundle in a follow-up email. Please include cost estimates for both Hosted and Dedicated options for the 2-week trial.

Jon / Asha 
- digging into the numbers from a technical perspective. High-level guidance and quick estimates below (will provide a short CSV with modeled numbers attached).

Assumptions we used for the estimate:
- Model family: optimized open-llm medium (approx 24B params) for balance of quality and latency. We can discuss a lighter 7B for lower latency.
- Input tokens (avg): 1,200; output tokens (avg): 400; total token budget per request ~1.6k.
- Baseline hardware: A100-class Dedicated node (or equivalent in Hosted optimized pool).

Latency considerations by context window:
- 2k context: expected p95 generation latency ~220-320 ms for the 1.6k token budget (with streaming enabled — time-to-first-token ~55-85 ms depending on warm KV cache).
- 8k context: we observe ~12-20% increase in end-to-end token generation time for similar token budgets due to KV cache memory lookups and attention overhead; p95 could rise to ~300-420 ms for equivalent requests (time-to-first-token ~80-140 ms).

Batching & concurrency tradeoffs:
- Aggressive batching improves throughput and lowers cost per token but increases tail latency. For your 350 ms p95 target, we recommend conservative batching (max batch size tuned to keep p95 within target) and prefer concurrency-level autoscaling rather than large batch windows.
- Streaming helps user-perceived latency (earlier first token) and allows partial responses while downstream processing continues, but it slightly increases CPU/PCIe overhead per request and can reduce overall throughput if not tuned.

Recommended pilot configuration:
- Run the 2k pilot on a single Dedicated pool with 2 worker nodes (reserve burst capacity + autoscale to 4 for campaign windows).
- Model: 24B quantized (int8) baseline; fallback to 7B for extreme latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Batching: dynamic batching with target batch latency cap of 25 ms.
- KV cache: pre-warm for the most common user prefixes for the pilot data set.

Attached: latency-estimate-table.csv (per-context window p50/p95 estimates across concurrency points). I'll schedule a perf run template and share the script so you can reproduce results in your environment.

If you'd like, we can also run a quick micro-benchmark during the trial window to validate time-to-first-token numbers (streaming) — I recommend we do that during a low-traffic window first.

Dylan
